storm.summary_layperson: No storms anywhere nearby tonight — just a cool, dry northerly breeze under mostly sunny skies, so the cove will see the same quiet evening as surrounding towns.
storm.local_effect_blurb: No marine-layer buffer: the air is already within 1°F of the 62°F Sound at 4 PM and drops well below water temperature after sunset, so the Sound offers no special protection this evening.
storm.detail_html:
Regional picture: KOKX radar shows no echoes to track anywhere in the approach sector, there are no NWS watches or warnings, and the atmosphere is completely stable — 0 J/kg of CAPE (no fuel for thunderstorms) with only about 4 kt of wind shear aloft. A cool high-pressure northerly flow covers the whole region.

Local modifiers: The Sound's usual protective effect comes from a cool, stable layer of air over the water when the water is at least ~5°F colder than the air. Tonight that gap is gone: Sound water is 61.7°F and the air is about 62–63°F at 4 PM, a difference of under 1°F. As the air cools after sunset (6:04 PM) it falls to roughly 53°F by 7 PM — colder than the water — so there is no stable marine layer at any point in the window. No sea breeze is running either; every coastal station is reporting a north-northeast wind.

Most likely outcome: Dry and quiet for the cove and everywhere around it. With no storms to deflect, the absence of a marine-layer buffer doesn't matter tonight — the cove behaves just like inland Westchester and Fairfield County.

What would change the call: Nothing in the current data points toward convection. Only a new radar echo developing upstream would warrant a re-check, and with zero instability that is very unlikely before tomorrow.

wind.regime_label: Moderate north-northeast gradient wind — no sea breeze in play
wind.tactics_blurb: Offshore north-northeasterly coming over land: expect puffs and holes with 10–20° swings rather than a steady line. Stay center, look upwind for dark-water puffs off the north shore, and tack on the big headers.
wind.tactics_detail_html:
Regime: This is a gradient-wind day, not a sea-breeze day. The air–water temperature difference is under 1°F (a sea breeze needs at least ~5°F), and no coastal station shows any southerly component. Airport anemometers around the western and central Sound (Bridgeport 12 kt, New Haven 13 gusting 19, Farmingdale 14) average about 11.6 kt from the NNE — a moderate gradient wind that doesn't depend on the sun, so it won't collapse at sunset.

Direction and cove geography: The ensemble median is NNE (~27°) and the HRRR model holds 15–18° through 6 PM, backing to about due north by 7 PM. Since this isn't a sea-breeze day, the sea-breeze direction correction does not apply; model and stations agree within 9°. North-northeast sits between the cove's two offshore characters: pure NE is usually laminar and fair, while N–NW comes over the houses and trees of the north shore and is gusty and shifty. Expect the puffier end of that as the wind backs toward north after sunset.

What you'll feel: RYC right now reads a 10-minute average of 8.5 kt with gusts to 17 but instantaneous lulls near 4 kt — a big gust/lull spread typical of offshore flow. Plan on roughly 7–8 kt at the 5 PM start, easing to 6–7 kt through sunset (6:04 PM) as the land cools and the boundary layer settles. That's a fully raceable breeze for most fleets early, getting marginal for heavier boats by 8–9 PM.

Tactics: No side is structurally favored in a northerly — the best average pressure is usually mid-cove, away from the immediate lee of the north and west shores. Shifts will be oscillating 10–20° puff to puff rather than persistent, so keep your head out of the boat, sail to the next dark patch upwind, and tack on the headers. Expect holes between puffs; don't get stuck near either shoreline.

Uncertainty: Model guidance only reached 7 PM on this run, so the 8–10 PM rows are an estimate extended from the evening trend (a moderate gradient wind usually softens 1–2 kt after dark rather than dying). Station directions are scattered (agreement 0.64), which fits the puffy offshore character more than any approaching boundary.

data_caveats: HRRR model guidance only available through 7 PM on this run (forecast hours 5–12 failed to download) — 8–10 PM wind rows are extrapolated from the evening trend.
Western LIS buoy 44040 offline (UConn ERDDAP fetch failed) — no over-water wind reading for the western Sound.
Groton, Islip, and Willimantic airport anemometers down — excluded from the wind ensemble.
